title: scroll
description: A wheel or two-finger scroll, at a position. The one input message that carries a DELTA rather than an absolute value, because scrolling has no absolute state to report. That is survivable on this channel because deltas commute: the host applies every scroll it receives in whatever order it arrives, and a lost one costs that much scroll distance and nothing else -- there is nothing to get stuck. The position fields are treated like a move's: applied only when this is the newest sample, so a late scroll never drags the cursor backwards. Coalesced by the sender to at most one per animation frame, deltas summed.

dx.description: Horizontal scroll in the sender's CSS pixels, DOM WheelEvent sign convention: positive scrolls right. Line and page deltas are normalised to pixels by the sender, one standard wheel notch = 100.

dy.description: Vertical scroll, same basis as dx: positive scrolls down (content moves up), as DOM deltaY does. Each host maps this to its native unit -- pixel scroll events on macOS, WHEEL_DELTA (120 per notch) on Windows.
